note.explanation: The stomach is an organ made of different tissues. Its epithelial tissue secretes mucus and gastric juice, while its smooth muscle layers contract and relax to mix food with gastric juice. Organ systems are groups of organs that work together to perform important body functions.
examples: The stomach is an organ in the digestive system.
The respiratory system includes the lungs, trachea, and bronchi.
note.checkAnswer: The epithelial tissue secretes mucus and gastric juice, and the smooth muscles mix food with gastric juice.
note.simple: An organ is made of tissues working together. An organ system is made of organs working together.

rationales: Correct: The blood circulatory system includes the heart, blood vessels, and blood.

Incorrect: Bones, cartilage, and tendons are listed as parts of the skeletal system.

Incorrect: The muscular system allows movement and locomotion.

written.text: What are the major roles of the epithelial tissue present in the stomach?
written.finalAnswer: It secretes mucus, which lines and protects the inner wall from acid, and gastric juice containing pepsinogen and hydrochloric acid for protein digestion.

Differentiate between the following:
i. Tissue and organ
written.finalAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells performing a specific function; an organ is made of different tissues working together to perform specific functions.

written.text: Describe the tissue composition of the stomach. How does each tissue contribute to the digestive function of the stomach?
written.finalAnswer: The stomach has epithelial tissue, connective tissue, three smooth muscle layers, and an outer connective tissue layer. The epithelial tissue secretes protective mucus and gastric juice; the connective tissue supports the stomach and contains blood vessels, nerves, and lymphatics; smooth muscles mix food with gastric juice; and the outer connective tissue encircles and supports the stomach.

rubric.why: The epithelial tissue's secretions protect the stomach wall and help digestion.
rubric.description: Describe epithelial tissue and its contribution.
rubric.how: Include mucus and gastric juice, with their protective and digestive roles.

rubric.why: The connective tissue supports the stomach and contains important structures.
rubric.how: Mention support and at least blood vessels, nerves, or lymphatics.

rubric.why: Muscle action mixes food with gastric juice.
rubric.description: Describe the muscle layers' digestive role.
rubric.how: State that smooth muscles contract and relax to mix food with gastric juice.

rubric.why: The final point completes the description of the stomach's outer tissue layer.
rubric.description: Give the correct overall tissue composition and outer layer role.
rubric.how: Name the outer connective tissue and state that it encircles and supports the stomach.

modelAnswer: The inner wall of the stomach is made up of glandular epithelial tissue.
It secretes mucus, which protects the inner wall from acid, and gastric juice containing pepsinogen and hydrochloric acid.
Connective tissue lies beneath the epithelial tissue; it provides structural support and contains blood vessels, nerves, and lymphatics.
There are three smooth muscle layers: outer longitudinal, middle circular, and inner oblique.
These muscles contract and relax to mix food with gastric juice.
The outer connective tissue encircles and supports the stomach.

written.text: How do the organ systems come together to form the human body?
written.finalAnswer: Organ systems are groups of organs that work together to perform particular functions. The skeletal, digestive, respiratory, muscular, nervous, and blood circulatory systems each perform their roles and work together to support and coordinate the body's functions.

rubric.why: This explains the relationship between organs and organ systems.
rubric.description: Explain what an organ system is.
rubric.how: State that organs work together in organ systems.

rubric.why: The skeletal system contributes structure, support, and protection.
rubric.description: Give a correct system example and role.
rubric.how: Name the skeletal system and describe one of its roles.

rubric.why: Examples show that different organ systems have distinct functions.
rubric.how: Name a system and connect it to its role.

rubric.why: This shows how systems contribute to the body's overall functioning.
rubric.description: Conclude by explaining the combined contribution of systems.
rubric.how: Explain that the nervous system coordinates and controls functions while the circulatory system transports substances.

modelAnswer: An organ system is a group of organs that work together to perform particular functions.
The skeletal system provides structure, support, and protection and allows movement with the muscles.
The digestive system digests food and absorbs digested food, while the respiratory system exchanges oxygen and carbon dioxide.
The muscular system allows movement and locomotion.
The nervous system coordinates and controls body functions through nerve impulses.
The blood circulatory system transports oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products throughout the body.
Together, these organ systems perform the functions needed by the human body.

written.text: Evaluate the importance of organ systems working in harmony and predict the consequences of a failure in one system on the others.
written.finalAnswer: Organ systems work together to perform body functions. For example, the respiratory system exchanges gases and the blood circulatory system transports oxygen and carbon dioxide. If one system fails, related functions in other systems can be affected; for example, failure of the respiratory system would disrupt the supply of oxygen to the blood and the transport of oxygen to body cells.

rubric.why: This establishes why systems working together matters.
rubric.description: State the importance of systems working together.
rubric.how: Explain that systems coordinate or work together to perform body functions.

rubric.how: Use the respiratory and blood circulatory systems and describe their roles.

rubric.why: This predicts that system failure can have effects beyond the failed system.
rubric.description: State a consequence of system failure.
rubric.how: Explain that a failure can disrupt functions involving other systems.

rubric.why: This provides a specific, biologically relevant consequence.
rubric.description: Give a concrete example of the consequences.
rubric.how: Explain how respiratory failure can interfere with oxygen reaching the blood and body cells.

modelAnswer: Organ systems work together to perform the functions of the body.
For example, the respiratory system exchanges oxygen and carbon dioxide between the body and environment.
The blood circulatory system transports oxygen throughout the body.
If the respiratory system fails, the exchange of gases is disrupted.
This can reduce the oxygen transported in the blood to body cells and affect other body functions.

examTips: Short questions may ask for the function of an organ, a tissue in the stomach, or a named organ system.
For stomach questions, name the tissue and state its function. Include the substances secreted by epithelial tissue when asked about its roles.
For a longer stomach question, cover all four components: epithelial tissue, connective tissue, the three smooth muscle layers, and outer connective tissue.
For organ-system questions, name the system and connect it to its function; avoid giving a list of names without explaining what they do.

example.question: Describe how the tissues of the stomach help it perform its functions.
example.answer: Epithelial tissue protects the inner wall and secretes gastric juice; connective tissue supports the stomach; smooth muscles mix food with gastric juice; and outer connective tissue encircles and supports the stomach.

explain.title: Organs have particular functions
explain.body: “Various organs are present in human body, each with specific functions.” For example, “The heart is a muscular organ that pumps blood throughout the body.” The lungs exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide, and the brain coordinates organs, thinking, and decision-making.

explain.title: The stomach is made of tissues
explain.body: “Stomach is an important organ of the digestive system. It is responsible for the partial digestion of proteins. It also stores food.” Its epithelial tissue secretes mucus and gastric juice; connective tissue provides support; and smooth muscle layers mix food with gastric juice.

explain.title: Stomach tissues have different jobs
explain.body: The epithelial tissue secretes mucus that protects the inner wall from acid, as well as gastric juice with pepsinogen and hydrochloric acid. Connective tissue lies beneath it and contains blood vessels, nerves, and lymphatics. The outer connective tissue encircles and supports the stomach.

explain.title: Muscles mix food in the stomach
explain.body: “There are three layers of smooth muscles: the outer longitudinal layer, the middle circular layer, and the inner oblique layer.” These muscles contract and relax to mix food with gastric juice.

explain.title: Organ systems work through their organs
explain.body: An organ system includes organs that carry out related functions. The digestive system digests food and absorbs it; the respiratory system exchanges gases; the nervous system coordinates and controls body functions; and the blood circulatory system transports oxygen, nutrients, hormones, and waste products.

mistakes: Do not say that the stomach has only muscle tissue; it also has epithelial tissue, connective tissue, and an outer connective tissue layer.
Do not confuse the jobs of mucus and gastric juice: mucus protects the inner wall, while gastric juice is involved in protein digestion.
Do not leave out the middle circular or inner oblique layer when naming the stomach's three smooth muscle layers.
Do not confuse an organ with an organ system: the stomach is an organ, while the digestive system includes several organs.
When describing a system, do not give only its name; state its function as well.
